fixes.explanation: Close, because Aaron's family does serve at the tabernacle. Aaron, the priest, had sons, and one of them, Ithamar, shows up later in this chapter (Numbers 7:8). Exodus 28:1 names Aaron's sons as Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. But the men presenting this offering are called "…the leaders of Israel, the heads of their families…" the tribal leaders who supervised the registration (Numbers 7:2). They are the givers here, not the priests.

That's the one. The text says they brought "…six covered carts and twelve oxen…" (Numbers 7:3). That's an ox from each leader and a cart from every two leaders, so the math works out clean. Twelve oxen and six carts showing up at once is not a quiet delivery.

The number is right, but the gifts are off. The leaders brought "…six covered carts and twelve oxen…" (Numbers 7:3). No tents and no camels are in this list. They presented the carts and oxen before the tabernacle, and that's the whole gift.

Right on. The LORD tells Moses, "Accept these gifts from them, that they may be used in the work of the Tent of Meeting." (Numbers 7:5). Then He says to give them to the Levites, and Moses does (Numbers 7:6). I know a lot of gifts that end up in a closet, but these ones get a job.

I see why you'd think so, with an altar right there. But the LORD says the gifts "…may be used in the work of the Tent of Meeting." (Numbers 7:5). Then Moses gives the carts and oxen to the Levites (Numbers 7:6). Nothing here says to offer them on the altar.

Not quite, friend. The LORD says to give the gifts to the Levites, "…to each man according to his service." (Numbers 7:5). That means no equal slices like one cookie handed to every person no matter the job. Each gets what the work calls for.

That's him. The text says it was "…all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest." (Numbers 7:8). The Merarites got four carts and eight oxen, and somebody had to keep an eye on that herd.

Good guess, since Eleazar is another son of Aaron (Exodus 28:1). But the text names a different son. It says the carts and oxen were "…all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest." (Numbers 7:8). Mixing up two brothers is easy to do, and I once mixed up two whisks.

Nice try, but the text never mentions carts of their own. The reason it gives is that the Kohathites "…were to carry on their shoulders the holy objects for which they were responsible." (Numbers 7:9). That's the reason, so look to their shoulder-carrying work and not to any carts they might own.

Good thought, since the altar is the star of this chapter. But the text puts Moses inside the Tent of Meeting, and he heard the voice "…from between the two cherubim above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony." (Numbers 7:89). So the voice isn't in the courtyard. It's from between the cherubim above the mercy seat.
